input.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
input.rationale: Governing law is Arizona, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so the clause fails both the preferred and fallback positions. In addition, Section 19 subjects all Disputes to mandatory binding arbitration under the U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules rather than to a court forum, and there is no venue or jurisdiction provision anywhere in the Agreement. We have therefore moved the governing law to New York and converted the arbitration mechanic into exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with the customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out, and conformed the Section 19 heading so no arbitration mechanic is left dangling.

mappings.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.

proposal.summary: Move governing law to New York and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive New York County court jurisdiction
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the governing law from Arizona to New York and replaced the mandatory arbitration mechanic with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County (preserving temporary injunctive relief elsewhere), as our playbook requires an accepted governing law and a court forum. Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London would also be acceptable.

ops.oldText: the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

ops.oldText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com). Any award or order rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed as a judgment or order in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction, which includes within the federal judicial district of the residence of the party against whom such award or order was entered.
ops.newText: will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York over the merits, and each party irrevocably submits to the jurisdiction of such courts; provided that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction.
